Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. File | Photo Credit: PTI
Security was tightened at Delhi’s Mandir Marg police station on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), ahead of the appearance of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka before a Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) court for verification of their sureties, in compliance with the conditions imposed at the time of their release from judicial custody last month.
The two had last appeared before the SEM Assistant Commissioner of Police Ritu Raj on October 23, two days after being released from Tihar jail following seven days in judicial custody. They were directed to return on November 17 for verification of their sureties and the accompanying documents.
During their October 23 appearance, Mr. Das was also asked to furnish a verifiable document corroborating his present residential address in Delhi, as he had failed to provide any document establishing the same.
The SEM court is examining compliance with the conditions attached to their release, including verification of their sureties and supporting documents.
At the time of their release on October 21, the two had furnished personal and surety bonds and submitted written undertakings before the SEM that they would not call for any protest at Jantar Mantar as long as it remained a denotified protest site. They also assured the court that they would not engage in any activity that could breach peace.
They were directed to appear on every hearing date and comply with the conditions specified in their bonds and undertakings.

The proceedings stem from two cases registered on October 13 at the Connaught Place and Parliament Street police stations after 14 CJP members entered Jantar Mantar through private premises and obstructed police personnel. The cases involve allegations of trespass, disobeying a government order and obstructing police personnel on duty, among other charges. They were transferred to the Delhi Police Crime Branch on October 20. The two leaders also appeared before the Crime Branch Branch in Rajouri Garden on November 5, 2026 after being summoned for questioning in connection with cases.
Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka were detained on October 13 and remanded to five days of judicial custody the following day. Their custody was extended by another two days on October 19. They were released on October 21 after the SEM court accepted their personal and surety bonds and recorded their written undertakings.

While Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka were remanded to judicial custody for allegedly violating an earlier peace bond they had signed, Mr. Shinde was released after furnishing a bond.
